item.title: Favourite pizza?: Re: Favourite pizza?
item.content:encoded:
The answer is simple, people who dislike pineapple pizza have defective tastebuds.

Close second for me is pepperoni, jalapeno, and mushroom followed by supreme(heavy on the peppers and mushrooms.)

item.title: Favourite pizza?: Re: Favourite pizza?
item.content:encoded: I live in a land bereft of good pizza places right now and it hurts my soul. Calgary had a really nice couple of places though. One, Mannie's, went out of business after being bought and dropping in quality quite a bit. Another, Niko's, is still around, and I highly recommend it to anyone living thereabouts.

item.title: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?: Re: Any scp articles suggestions for someone new to scp?
item.content:encoded:
Make sure to check out the Site-Generated Recommended Reading thread, the User-Curated Lists, and the Top Rated New Pages! I've also got a list of personal recommendations on my sandbox site.

SCP-093 is pretty in-depth, SCP-1746's pretty quirky, and SCP-2922 is a very cool rabbit-hole.

item.title: There Is No First SCP Curse!: Re: There Is No First SCP Curse!
item.content:encoded:
Since the new Exploring Series video just dropped, I might as well point to SCP-4051 — no idea crit, very sparing draft crit, like ten different bad SCP stereotypes, currently at +236 with a supplement at +144. It also kinda started the Deepwell canon, which is very cool.

Point is, the Rule of Cool is very much a thing, and if you can get readers invested in a character and a setting, you can absolutely do anything.

also please stop asking if he kins spider-man

item.title: Site-Generated Recommended Reading: Re: Site-Generated Recommended Reading
item.content:encoded:
My picks:

SCP: - SCP-1762 - Where the dragons went

This article is really good, like really good. It doesn't require much knowledge of the foundation's lore, but it shows new readers that SCP's don't have to horror or violent, and it's just really, really sad. If you haven't read this read it.

Tale: -The stars do not wait for you.

While the tale has a fair few crosslinks, it is a good starting point for someone who wants to find some other articles and also just follow a damn good story.

item.title: What are your two favorite articles on the SCP wiki?: Re: What are your two favorite articles on the SCP wiki?
item.content:encoded:
SCP-999-J and Pelagic Society.

Both gave me uncontrollable laugh, and that's what really matter.

item.title: What are your two favorite articles on the SCP wiki?: Re: What are your two favorite articles on the SCP wiki?
item.content:encoded:
My favorite article on-site would have to be SCP-5375 - "Nobody and the Name Machine" The whole thing appealed to me, and as such, it is my favorite.

For second, that's tricky, but I would have to go with SCP-5160 - "Grandma Sheep believes in you!" Simple article, nice and short, loved it!

I would recommend both of these articles. Both are high quality and engaging to read through.
